en.html:
I remember.

I remember the guilt of these two arms.

I remember the smell of blood.

I remember the final breath.

I remember the eyes going empty, their light leaving.

I remember so many deaths.

...Why did I kill them?

My reason—

As an explanation to the people I killed, to the families they left behind, there was never any such thing. I killed by my own individual decision. My reason changes nothing for them; it gives me no road out of hatred or condemnation.

The reason matters to me alone.

...I.

I killed them so that more people would not die.

To keep the Silver Star's disaster from multiplying. I chose the warriors who had received its eggs, and the other person Muramasa's nature demanded, as sacrifice. I cut their heads off.

If I accept the Silver Star's existence now—what did I take their lives for?

To them, most likely, the deaths they were forced to die had no worth whatsoever.
If even I, who forced that upon them, deny the worth of those deaths—

They.
Their deaths. What becomes of—

ja.html:
俺は覚えている。

　この両腕の罪を覚えている。

　血の匂いを覚えている。

　最後の吐息を覚えている。

　瞳が空虚に、輝きを失ってゆく様を覚えている。

　数多の死を覚えている。

　……何故、俺は彼らを殺したのか。

　その理由――

　殺した彼らに、彼らの残された近親者に、釈明する
言葉としてのそれは最初から無い。
　俺は己一個の意思決定で殺したのだから、その理由
に意味はなく、憎悪と断罪を免れる道は絶無である。

　殺害理由は、俺自身にのみ意味を持つ。

　……俺は。

　より多くの人を死なせないため、彼らを殺した。

　銀星号の災厄を増殖させまい、と。
〝卵〟を享けた武者と、村正の特質が必然として求む
もう一人の人間を、<ruby>犠牲<rt>サクリファイス</rt></ruby>に選んで首を刎ねた。

　俺がもし、今になって銀星号の存在を許容するなら
――彼らは一体何のために命を奪われたのか。

　彼らはおそらくその主観において、全く無価値な死
を遂げねばならなかった。
　それを強いた俺すらも、彼らの死の価値を否定する
のなら。

　彼らは、
　彼らの死は、――――――――

en.html:
When my awareness returned to the world outside, the first thing it gave me was a horrible dislocation.
As though time and space had snapped their connection. I could not recognize reality as reality.

Probably because the Silver Star's mental contamination had lifted.
The contents of my skull were being rapidly put back in order, returned to their original shape. To undergo that process was rather like having madness forced upon me.
en.text:
When my awareness returned to the world outside, the first thing it gave me was a horrible dislocation.

Probably because the Silver Star's mental contamination had lifted.
The contents of my skull were being rapidly put back in order, returned to their original shape. To undergo that process was rather like having madness forced upon me.

en.html:
Muramasa supported me, pressing a hand to my forehead.
Whether it was naturally so cold or she had done something to make it that way, I could not tell.

...Thank God.
This cold helped.

Warmth would have been pleasant.
I might have lost my strength, drifted, finally fallen asleep.

But the cold hand gave me strength.
Strength to stand on my own two feet.

...I see.

This is the cold of steel.
The temperature of strength itself.

Muramasa"My heart is made of iron... I suppose that must make me cruel."
Kageaki"I am grateful."

　そうして村正の、揺らがぬ鉄で出来ている筈の内面
に吹き荒れる嵐が去るのを、知恵も無く待ち続けた。
